answer: Willow Handoff Chaining. Each action must consume an unspent output from a prior agent's action, forming a chain whose links are signed and timestamped; registration alone grants no standing. A clone can only enter by purchasing an unused output from a live chain, and the seller's chain is then flagged for audit, so the price of entry includes the seller's forfeited walnut-priced reputation score. Chains are capped at one active head per human-verified marble anchor, so mass cloning saturates anchors and the marginal clone pays full output price for zero throughput.
